items.title: Interview #99 Bob De Caux, Chief AI Officer at IFS
items.summary: Bob De Caux, Chief AI Officer at IFS, breaks down why the most dangerous moment for industrial AI comes after people start trusting it. He explains why agents still struggle when handed too much information, why guardrails against irreversible decisions matter far more than planning or memory, and why keeping live operational data out of external models is about uptime, not preference. Bob also dives into why chat will not replace the Gantt chart or the spreadsheet, how dispatchers who embraced automation still wanted an exceptions-based view to stay sharp, and the point where accountability moves from the company back to the vendor when a harness breaks. Finally, drawing on his early work modeling systems of ants, he warns that emergent failures between agents only appear at scale, and argues that LLMs will never solve forecasting and optimization on their own. items.title: How to Make AI-Translated Content Convert in Every Market - with Andrew Thomas of Acclaro
items.summary: Translating content into every language a company serves has become fast and inexpensive, but accurate translation does not ensure that content engages or converts in each market. In this episode, Andrew Thomas, Head of Marketing at Acclaro, explains why global content performance is a governance issue rather than a translation issue, and why leaders should judge localized content by the business outcome it was created to drive. He also covers testing new markets with AI-translated content before investing in local teams, building brand style guides and terminology into AI translation tools to curb shadow localization, and using automated quality checks to decide when an in-country expert needs to review content. This episode is sponsored by Acclaro AI can help you reach new markets faster, but how do you connect that investment to business results?
